title: Area-based Image Analysis Algorithm for Quantification of Macrophage-fibroblast Cocultures
protocol: Culture RAW264.7 macrophages at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 1.5 g/L sodium bicarbonate, and 5 µM β-mercaptoethanol.
Culture RAW264.7 cells at a density of 25,000 cells/cm² in a 5 mL cell culture flask with 1 mL of medium for monoculture imaging.
Culture NIH/3T3 cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.

For coculture imaging, culture RAW264.7 macrophages and NIH/3T3 fibroblasts together at a total density of 25,000 cells/cm² using coculture medium consisting of equal parts RAW264.7 medium and NIH/3T3 medium.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until they reach a viable cell density of 80% confluence.
Image cells with an inverted microscope equipped with a 40x objective.
Acquire all images in grayscale and export them as '.czi' files.
Export cell images to 8-bit TIFF format using ImageJ.
Store converted images in a local folder.
Transfer image files manually to the relevant MATLAB bin.
Run "monoculture.m" file for analyzing monoculture images.
Use imread('filename.tiff') to read the tiff image file.
Analyze images by opening by reconstruction using imopen().
Close by reconstruction using imerode() and imreconstruct().
Binarize the reconstructed images to pure black and pure white pixels using a percentile-based identification system.
Convert cells to a pure white pixel value of '255'.
Convert background and extraneous objects to a pure black pixel value of '0'.
Determine the maximum relevant pixel, defined as the largest pixel value comprising at least 0.5% of a given image.
Analyze pixel values for RAW264.7 macrophages.
Mark pixels within 4.5% of the maximum relevant pixel as cellular.
Implement an iterative procedure to correct erroneous binarization at the centers of bulbous cells, termed 'islands'.
Determine an initial guess for total cell coverage; 60% was used in this study.
Establish the relationship between cell number and cell coverage experimentally.
Determine variables 'Alpha' and 'kappa' based on the established relationship.
Determine the range of radii for macrophage cells based on experimental data.
Set [minradius, maxradius] to [30, 50].
Use imfindcircle function with the set parameters to detect circles in the image.
Calculate the average cell area by averaging the areas of detected circles.
Analyze at least 10 cells to ensure accurate area identification.
Count the total number of cell pixels within the image matrix.
Divide the number of cell pixels by the total number of pixels within the image to determine total cell coverage.
Divide the number of cell pixels by the average cell area to determine the total number of cells in the image.
Use the area-based method to obtain images of cells showing relative height variations.
Utilize the 'imshow()' function for each subimage.
Copy and paste the image file for analysis into the bin.
Enter the file name in the command: imread('filename.tiff').
Press run to start the program.
Conduct an analysis by opening the image using reconstruction.
Apply erosion followed by dilation to close the image by reconstruction.
Determine RAW264.7 cell counts and total cell coverage using two selective binarizations exploiting height differences between RAW264.7 and NIH/3T3 cells.
Guess an initial phi value and iterate until cell counts match closely with manual counts specific to the coculture.
Use phi = 3.2 for filtering images to contain only RAW264.7 cells selectively.
Analyze the watershed-transformed image without the phi parameter, detecting both macrophages and fibroblasts.
Acquire NIH/3T3 fibroblast data by selectively subtracting RAW264.7 cell pixels using standard thresholding and area-based quantification methods.
Determine the total number of NIH/3T3 pixels by subtracting the total number of cell pixels from the number of RAW264.7 pixels.
Calculate the coverage of NIH/3T3 cells by dividing the number of NIH/3T3 cell pixels by the total number of image pixels.
Calculate the coverage of RAW264.7 cells by dividing the number of RAW264.7 cell pixels by the total number of image pixels.
